# `Money`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Money — currency-typed Money on `Ipe.Decimal`.

`Money` carries both magnitude and ISO-4217 currency code in one typed
value.  The `Money` / `Currency` ADTs and the pure combinators (arithmetic,
comparison, percent, `currencyCode`, `parseCurrency`) live here as Ipê
source; the currency-property table, formatter, fair-split `allocate`, and
FX rate registry route through the guarded `Money_*` runtime kernels via
point-free `Kernel.kernel` aliases (each wrapper converts its `Currency` arg to
an ISO 4217 code first, since the kernels take the code as a `String`).

## `add`

```ipe
add : Money -> Money -> Result Error Money
```

Add two Money values. Returns `Err` when the currencies differ — a
mismatch is a typed error, not a silent wrong value. Convert both to a
common currency first (via `Money.convert`) if needed.

## `sub`

```ipe
sub : Money -> Money -> Result Error Money
```

Subtract two Money values. Returns `Err` when the currencies differ — a
mismatch is a typed error, not a silent wrong value. Convert both to a
common currency first (via `Money.convert`) if needed.

```ipe
mul : Decimal -> Money -> Money
```

Multiply by a scalar (Decimal). Currency carries through.

## `allocate`

```ipe
allocate : Int -> Money -> List Money
```

Allocate a Money value across N parts as evenly as possible, with any
residue distributed toward zero (positive totals step up, negative totals
step down) so the returned parts sum to the input exactly.

Returns [] when parts <= 0, and (via the kernel's guard) when parts exceeds
100k or the amount overflows — the cap prevents a caller-controlled `parts`
from exhausting memory / the call stack.

  allocate 3 ($100.00)  -> [$33.34, $33.33, $33.33]
  allocate 3 (-$1.00)   -> [-$0.34, -$0.33, -$0.33]
  allocate 0 ($100.00)  -> []

## `sumOf`

```ipe
sumOf : Currency -> List Money -> Result Error Money
```

Sum a list of Money values for a given currency. Returns `Err` if any
element has a different currency — a mismatch is a typed error. Convert
all elements to the target currency first (via `Money.convert`) if needed.

## `format`

```ipe
format : Money -> String
```

Default symbol-prefixed form: "$12.34", "¥1234" (JPY). The amount is
rounded half-away-from-zero to the currency's minor units (so "$2.545"
renders "$2.55", not the truncated "$2.54").

## `formatWithCode`

```ipe
formatWithCode : Money -> String
```

ISO-code suffix form: "12.34 USD". Preferred for B2B. Same
half-away-from-zero rounding as `format`.

## `knownCurrency`

```ipe
knownCurrency : Currency -> Bool
```

True for every named Currency variant (USD, JPY, BTC, …).
False ONLY for `CurrencyRaw _`. The named variants are enumerated as one
or-pattern so adding a Currency variant forces an update here instead of
silently reporting as known.

## `isKnownCode`

```ipe
isKnownCode : String -> Bool
```

Check whether an ISO 4217 code string is a recognised currency, via the
runtime currency table (the single source of truth for known codes).

## `parseCurrency`

```ipe
parseCurrency : String -> Maybe Currency
```

Parse an ISO 4217 currency code string into a `Currency`.
Returns `Nothing` for any unrecognised code — the caller must handle
the absent case explicitly. Use `CurrencyRaw` directly when you need
a passthrough for codes outside the known set.

## `setRate`

```ipe
setRate : Currency -> Currency -> Decimal -> Result Error ()
```

Register an FX rate. Rejects a non-positive rate; auto-registers the
inverse so consumers need not set both directions.

## `getRate`

```ipe
getRate : Currency -> Currency -> Result Error Decimal
```

Look up a registered rate (identity for from == to; missing → Err).
